links.targetTitle: The Resilience Fund can be used when Sky itself is the targe

title: The Purpose System's only binding rule is a ten percent floor for direct and specific impact
content:
A.2.12 establishes the Purpose System "which aims to fund open-source AI and software projects that benefit the Sky Ecosystem and public good." A.2.12.1 is a placeholder — the Section "must define the elements and infrastructure necessary to implement the Purpose System effectively," including "a process for allocating purpose funds to individual Agents" — so neither the funding source, the allocation mechanism, nor the selection process exists yet.

Against that emptiness, A.2.12.2 is fully operative: "[a]t all times, at least 10% of the Purpose System funds must be used for more direct and specific impact solutions."

The ordering is informative. Of everything the Purpose System needs, the provision written first is a constraint on how the money may be split. That suggests a known tension the framers wanted settled before the machinery existed: open-source AI and software funding is diffuse and slow to show results, and a fund of that kind can spend indefinitely without anything legible to point at. The floor guarantees a visible minority of spending goes to direct, specific outcomes.

"At all times" makes it a continuous constraint rather than a target measured at year end, so the ratio must hold through every allocation decision. The undefined term is "more direct and specific impact solutions," which has no definition anywhere in the Article — whoever eventually builds the allocation process inherits both a binding ratio and the discretion to decide what counts toward it.
description: The funding section is still an empty mandate to define allocation infrastructure, yet a hard minimum already stops the fund being spent entirely on diffuse open-source work.
